title: I built a 3D RTS inspired by Stick War: Legacy in less than a week using AI
author: unity_sergey
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I decided to experiment with AI-assisted game development after seeing how popular the topic has become on YouTube.

I took inspiration from the old mobile strategy game Stick War: Legacy and tried to recreate its core gameplay in 3D.

**My workflow:**

* Unity as the game engine.
* Cursor ($20/month) for AI-assisted coding.
* Claude Opus to build the initial prototype.
* Grok 4.6 for most of the remaining development.
* ChatGPT to help design the UI layout.
* Suno to generate the soundtrack.

Instead of asking AI to make the entire game in one prompt, I built it incrementally, adding features and testing them along the way.

I was surprised by how much functionality appeared in the initial prototype, including unit grouping, double-click selection of all units of the same type, and other RTS mechanics I hadn't explicitly requested.

Once the core gameplay was ready, I focused on the visuals. AI generated placeholder graphics using primitive shapes, while I reused character models, castle models, and environmental assets from my previous projects.

**The game includes:**

* A 16-level campaign with difficulty settings.
* Survival mode with endless waves of enemies.
* Online multiplayer battles.
* A level editor with customizable landscapes, weather, time of day, units, and objects.

I also generated the soundtrack using Suno.

The entire project took less than a week. I spent $20 on Cursor and used approximately 30% of my monthly usage allowance. I also paid Steam's $100 app fee, bringing my total expenses to around $120.

The game is free to play.

I'd especially appreciate feedback on the gameplay and the overall experience.
